newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse maintains a high trend.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse maintains a high trend.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse ended slightly higher on Tuesday due mainly to a rise by Societe Nationale d'Investissement shares, analysts said.
The all-share index, which rose above the 400-point mark for the first time on Monday, continued its upward trend to close at 400.47 points.
SNI, which has interests in more than 40 companies and a market capitalisation of more than 5.5 billion dirhams, rose two dirhams to 562 dirhams.
Ciments de l'Oriental, the most liquid share, has gained four dirhams since the beginning of the month, while Ciments Artificiels de Meknes rose 11 dirhams compared with the previous session.

CADEM, which is a subsidiary of cement giant Lafarge Maroc, will probably score a higher closing price under persistent rumours that it will be delisted in the near future, stockbrkers said. CADEM is expected to be replaced by the largest Lafarge Maroc unit, cement firm Cinouca. The bourse turnover reached 7.5 million dirhams, up from 3.5 million dirhams on Monday. ($1= 8.6 dirhams)
